title: html5lib and libxml2 renditions of the S0/S0-R2 pages are content-identical
question: Can later spikes, and phase 0 under html5lib (D4 M01), use the references built on the libxml2 renditions?
method: code/s1g_html5lib_identity.py compared, for the seven pages the S0/S0-R2 units use, the html5lib rendition with the stored libxml2 one: canonical text, segments (kind, start, end, attributes, tree) and provisional sentences; and checked a fresh libxml2 run reproduces the stored files. Decision by the design authority (2026-10-28): `attrs.sourceline` is a parser-dependent diagnostic outside the rendition contract (D1 §3.2), so content identity excludes it.

outputs.role: per page, unit and locator comparison

conclusion: Content-identical on all seven pages; only keys differ, as the rendition key hashes the parser. Spikes keep scoring against the reproducible libxml2 renditions; phase 0 html5lib renditions take the references by re-storing the quote-citing model-facing batches.
